cards.explanation: The answer is the leaders of the people. The text says, "Now the leaders of the people settled in Jerusalem…" (Nehemiah 11:1). The rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live there too, while the other nine stayed in their own towns. I picture those leaders unpacking boxes in the holy city, friends.

The answer is True. The text says the rest of the people "…cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in the holy city of Jerusalem…" (Nehemiah 11:1). Casting lots was a way of picking, kind of like drawing names, friends. The other nine were to dwell in their own towns.

The answer is one. One out of ten gets picked to live in Jerusalem, "…while the remaining nine were to dwell in their own towns." (Nehemiah 11:1). Picture ten people at a table and only one gets the move, friends. I'd be that one nervously checking if my mustache fits through the door.

The answer is holy. The text calls it "…the holy city of Jerusalem…" (Nehemiah 11:1). That's the name the writer gives the place these people are moving to, friends. I'd say that's quite the address to write on a moving box.

The answer is that the people bless them. The text says, "And the people blessed all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem." (Nehemiah 11:2). These men volunteered, and the people blessed every one of them, friends. I bet that felt like the cheer you'd get for saying "I'll bring the cookies."
